examples.trans: Yes, that was our gift to Mom for her birthday!

examples.text: Вика, ну какая разница, подарок от невестки!
examples.trans: Vika, well what difference does it make, a gift from her daughter-in-law!

examples.text: Это тебе подарок.
examples.trans: This is a present for you.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'mum', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Вика, уже завтра к нам приезжает мама!
examples.trans: Vika, Mom is coming to visit us tomorrow already!

examples.text: Надо ещё решить, где мы разместим маму.
examples.trans: We also need to decide where we will put Mom.

examples.text: Купи маме цветы и сладости к чаю.
examples.trans: Buy flowers for Mom and sweets for tea.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Мы тебе что, похожи на агентство жилья?
examples.trans: What do we look like to you, a housing agency?

examples.text: Я тебя ночью на улицу точно не выгоню.
examples.trans: I definitely will not kick you out onto the street at night.

examples.text: Мальчики, я сейчас отъеду на пару часов.
examples.trans: Boys, I am going to step out right now for a couple of hours.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'day', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Да, это наш подарок маме на день рождения!
examples.trans: Yes, that was our gift to Mom for her birthday!

examples.text: Добрый день!
examples.trans: Good afternoon!

examples.text: Я позвоню на днях.
examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'birth' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Да, это наш подарок маме на день рождения!
examples.trans: Yes, that was our gift to Mom for her birthday!

examples.text: У него сегодня день рождения!
examples.trans: It is his birthday today!

examples.text: С днём рождения!
examples.trans: Happy birthday!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'мнить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to remember'.

examples.text: Вика, ты же помнишь, как мы его послали?
examples.trans: Vika, surely you remember how we sent it to her?

examples.text: Ты помнишь?
examples.trans: Do you remember?

examples.text: Я всё помню.
examples.trans: I remember everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('we') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Вика, уже завтра к нам приезжает мама!
examples.trans: Vika, Mom is coming to visit us tomorrow already!

examples.text: Она просто решила сделать нам большой сюрприз.
examples.trans: She simply decided to give us a big surprise.

examples.text: У нас дома сейчас такой ужасный бардак!
examples.trans: We have such a terrible mess at home right now!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'слать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to sent'.

examples.text: Вика, ты же помнишь, как мы его послали?
examples.trans: Vika, surely you remember how we sent it to her?

examples.text: Викочка, здравствуйте, как же я рада вас видеть!
examples.trans: Vikochka, hello, how glad I am to see you!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'constantly'.

examples.text: Я его постоянно ношу, ты у меня умница!
examples.trans: I wear it constantly, you are such a clever girl!

examples.text: Что ты постоянно боишься?
examples.trans: What are you constantly afraid of?

examples.text: Он постоянно опаздывал на работу.
examples.trans: He was constantly late for work.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to carry'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я его постоянно ношу, ты у меня умница!
examples.trans: I wear it constantly, you are such a clever girl!

examples.text: Он носил радиаторы.
examples.trans: He was carrying radiators.

examples.text: Аркадий носит очки.
examples.trans: Arkady wears glasses.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Мне кажется, у женщин есть какое-то оружие.
examples.trans: It seems to me that women have some kind of weapon.

examples.text: У тебя вдруг снова появляются забытые чувства.
examples.trans: Forgotten feelings suddenly appear in you again.

examples.text: У нас дома сейчас такой ужасный бардак!
examples.trans: We have such a terrible mess at home right now!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'clever person', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я его постоянно ношу, ты у меня умница!
examples.trans: I wear it constantly, you are such a clever girl!

examples.text: Вот и умница!
examples.trans: Good girl/boy!

examples.text: Вот и умница, работа лечит всё!
examples.trans: Good girl, work cures everything!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'oh', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ой, я же ещё руки с дороги не помыла!
examples.trans: Oh, I have not even washed my hands from the trip yet!

examples.text: Ой, Вика, я где-то зацепилась, нитка поползла!
examples.trans: Oh, Vika, I snagged it somewhere, a thread has started to run!

examples.text: Ой, Викочка, а что с тобой вдруг случилось?
examples.trans: Oh, Vikochka, what suddenly happened to you?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.

examples.text: Надо ещё решить, где мы разместим маму.
examples.trans: We also need to decide where we will put Mom.

examples.text: Ой, я же ещё руки с дороги не помыла!
examples.trans: Oh, I have not even washed my hands from the trip yet!

examples.text: То есть я у нас ещё и прекрасно готовлю?
examples.trans: So I also cook wonderfully in our house?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'hand', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ой, я же ещё руки с дороги не помыла!
examples.trans: Oh, I have not even washed my hands from the trip yet!

examples.text: Что вы делаете, немедленно уберите ваши руки!
examples.trans: What are you doing, take your hands off me immediately!

examples.text: Вика, да у тебя же просто золотые руки!
examples.trans: Vika, why, you simply have golden hands!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'road', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Это плохая дорога.
examples.trans: This is a bad road.

examples.text: Кто строит дороги?
examples.trans: Who builds the roads?

examples.text: Какая разница, кто будет строить дороги?
examples.trans: What does it matter who builds the roads?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Прости, но оставить тебя здесь я не смогу.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but I will not be able to keep you here.

examples.text: Хорошо, я всё сделаю, не волнуйся.
examples.trans: All right, I will do everything, do not worry.

examples.text: И смотри, маме про себя не говори!
examples.trans: And mind you, do not tell Mom about yourself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'мыть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wash', forming an aspectual pair with 'мыть'.

examples.text: Ой, я же ещё руки с дороги не помыла!
examples.trans: Oh, I have not even washed my hands from the trip yet!

examples.text: Надо помыть пол.
examples.trans: The floor needs washing.

examples.text: Я помою посуду.
examples.trans: I'll wash the dishes.
